chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim al-Bajalī, from Sālim Abī Khadījah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man asked, while I was present, and said: Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying al-ʿAṣr, while some of them are praying al-Ẓuhr. So he said: “I instructed them to do this. If they all prayed at one single time, they would be recognized and then seized by their necks.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: our companions, referring to the followers associated with the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.أَمَرْتُهُمْ: I instructed them, indicating deliberate guidance from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, where the companions were observed praying
key_terms.فَأُخِذُوا بِرِقَابِهِمْ: then they would be seized by their necks, meaning apprehended harshly
key_terms.لَعُرِفُوا: they would be recognized or identified

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instruct some companions to pray at different times in the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Imam عليه السلام deliberately instructed variation in the apparent prayer timing among his companions. The purpose was protective concealment, so that if they all acted identically at one time, they would be identified and persecuted.
